validated_results.title: Higher insoluble fiber intake is associated with a lower risk of prostate cancer: results from the PLCO cohort.
validated_results.reason: This prospective cohort analysis of the PLCO trial evaluates the association between insoluble dietary fiber intake and incident prostate cancer risk.

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 54,336 men were recruited, including 6,414 PCa patients. The average age of participants in the PCa and control groups was 63.4±5.1 and 62.5±5.3, respectively.

cases.excerpt: Therefore, this study examined the relationship between fiber intake and the risk of PCa by using data from Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial. A total of 54,336 participants in the United States, consisting of 6,414 patients with PCa, were included in this study.

effect_size.excerpt: Compared with individuals in the lowest quartile, individuals in the highest quartile of insoluble fiber intake had a significantly lower risk of PCa (aHR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.78–0.98). By contrast, no significant associations were detected between total fiber intake (aHR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.80–1.01) or soluble fiber intake (aHR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.80–1.02).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Compared with individuals in the lowest quartile, individuals in the highest quartile of insoluble fiber intake had a significantly lower risk of PCa (aHR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.78–0.98).

p_value.excerpt: As shown in Table 2 , compared with those of subjects in the lowest quartile of insoluble fiber (Q1), the aHRs of PCa risk were 0.97 (95% CI, 0.90–1.05; P = 0.453), 0.97 (95% CI, 0.90–1.06; P = 0.526), and 0.87 (95% CI, 0.78–0.98; P = 0.016) for groups Q2, Q3, and Q4, respectively.

comparison.excerpt: Compared with individuals in the lowest quartile, individuals in the highest quartile of insoluble fiber intake had a significantly lower risk of PCa (aHR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.78–0.98).
